mainKeyword: best countertop dishwashers with water tanks
guideTitle: Best Countertop Dishwashers With Water Tanks (2026)
metaDescription: Six tank-fed countertop dishwashers compared by tank volume, fill method and drain routine: 6L, 5L and removable-tank designs for no-plumbing kitchens.
expertTake: The Comfee Miniplus is the best overall because its 6 liter tank and 10.5 inch plate clearance give the roomiest tank design here. The ChuMaste is the value pick for one or two people. Anyone who runs several loads a day should skip tank models and choose a faucet-fed unit.
introParagraphs: A water tank turns a dishwasher into a self-contained appliance. There is no faucet adaptor, no pressure fitting and no plumbing to fight with, which is why tank models dominate rentals, dorms and campers.

The catch is that the tank is both the water supply and the limit on a load. Its volume, the way it fills and the way it empties decide how pleasant the machine is to live with, and those details vary more than the program lists do.

products.name: Comfee Miniplus Countertop Dishwasher, 6L Tank, 10.5 in Plates
products.description:
The Miniplus carries the largest tank in this guide at 6 liters, which is about 1.6 gallons. That extra volume matters in a machine where the tank sets the ceiling on a load. The interior is also described as bigger than a typical mini washer, with room for a 10.5 inch plate, a size that rules out many competitors.

Five programs cover Normal, Rapid, Hygiene, Fruit and Glass, with two extra functions on top. Compared with the 5 liter Hermitlux below it gains a liter of water and a defined plate clearance, but it lacks a Self-Clean program. It also lacks a faucet connection, so everything depends on the pour.

Pour from a jug with a spout, fill to the line and close the door. After the cycle, drain the leftover water, rinse the tank and leave the lid open so it dries. A tank that stays wet between loads grows slime and odor faster than a dry one.
products.bestFor: Small households that want the roomiest tank and plate clearance.
pros: 6 liter tank is the largest in this guide
Interior accepts plates up to 10.5 inches
Hygiene cycle heats water for dirtier loads
Goes anywhere with power and a drain path
cons: Manual fill and drain for every load

products.name: Sunvivipro 18 Inch Countertop Dishwasher, 152 oz Removable Tank

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: 6 presets, Standard and Quick among them

products.description:
This is the only removable tank in the group. A 152 ounce reservoir, about 4.5 liters, lifts out of the machine so you fill it at the faucet rather than pouring from a jug at the counter. That solves the common complaint about tank models, which is spilling near the electrics while balancing a jug.

Six presets include Standard and Quick, and the machine also takes a faucet supply for dual use. The tank is smaller than the Miniplus' 6 liters, and the footprint of 17.7 by 17.3 inches is a little larger than the 5 liter cubes. Plates up to about 10 inches fit.

The removable tank creates its own chores. Check the seal each time you seat it, because a half-seated tank is the most likely leak source. Rinse and dry the tank weekly to prevent slime, and do not leave water standing in it between loads.
products.bestFor: Anyone who finds pouring from a jug awkward and wants a tank that lifts out.

products.name: Hermitlux Countertop Dishwasher, 5L Tank, Glass Door, 4 Settings
products.description:
The Hermitlux pairs a 5 liter tank with a stated capacity of four place settings, which is the clearest pairing of tank size and load in the group. A transparent glass door lets you watch the spray arm and see whether a load is clean, a feature that helps new owners learn how to stack the rack.

Five programs include Standard Cleaning, Fast Cleaning and ECO, and the body measures 16.85 by 16.73 by 18.03 inches on 120V power. Compared with the Miniplus it has a smaller tank but a stated capacity, while the newer seven-program Hermitlux in other guides adds Self-Clean and Glass cycles that this one lacks.

The door deserves care. Glass shows spots, so wipe it weekly, and watch the seal for grit. As with every tank model, empty the reservoir when the machine is idle, and keep the filter clean.

products.name: Euhomy 8-Program Countertop Dishwasher, 5L Tank, 167 F Wash
products.description:
This Euhomy puts a high-temperature wash on a tank model. The listing quotes 167 F and eight programs, and it says the machine handles more than 30 items with a built-in 5 liter tank. Heat is the useful variable in a tank machine, because small tanks mean little water volume and heat does more of the work.

Eight programs give the widest list among the tank models here, but the claim of 30 plus items is a piece count, not place settings. Against the Miniplus it offers hotter water and more programs at the cost of a smaller tank, and against the Hermitlux it gives up the stated four-setting capacity.

Because the wash runs hot, keep thin plastics out. After each run drain the tank, wipe the chamber and leave the door open. If the machine will sit for days, empty and dry the reservoir.

products.name: ChuMaste Countertop Dishwasher, Water Tank, 5 Programs, Compact

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: Normal, Quick, Eco, Baby Care, Fruit

products.description:
The ChuMaste is the lowest cost option in this lineup and the smallest in plan view at 16.54 by 16.54 inches. Five programs cover Normal, Quick, Eco, Baby Care and Fruit, and the listing says the machine can also dry and store tableware. A built-in tank keeps it independent of the faucet.

It is positioned for small households, so expect loads smaller than the Hermitlux or the Miniplus. The listing is less specific about the tank volume and the temperature, so check the manual for both before relying on the Baby Care program for bottles. The reward is a low entry cost and a compact cube.

A light-duty machine needs light-duty habits. Rinse plates first, run Quick for cups and bowls and keep the filter clean. Someone who wants to see whether the tank format suits them will find it a gentle first step.

products.name: Comfee Portable Countertop Dishwasher, 1.32 Gal Tank, 6 Programs

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: Normal, Rapid, Hygiene, Fruit, Glass, Air Refresh

products.description:
The original Comfee tank model uses a 1.32 gallon tank, which converts to about 5 liters, so it is the same size as the other 5 liter cubes despite sounding smaller. Six programs include Normal, Rapid, Hygiene, Fruit, Glass and Air Refresh, and every program uses 360 degree spray coverage.

Its unusual feature is Air Refresh, a circulation mode that helps the chamber and dishes stay dry and fresh. Tanks left wet are the main source of odor in this class, so a built-in routine for airing the chamber has real value. The Hygiene cycle reaches 158 F, which is cooler than the Euhomy's quoted 167 F.

Use Air Refresh after cleaning cycles and leave the door cracked. Empty the tank before storing the machine, and rinse the filter every few loads.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Tank sizes appear in three units. The Comfee 1.32 gallon tank equals about 5 liters, the Sunvivipro's 152 ounces equals about 4.5 liters, and the Miniplus lists 6 liters, which is about 1.6 gallons. A larger tank allows a fuller load before you refill. Convert to liters before comparing.

Pouring from a jug is the common method, but a removable tank like the Sunvivipro fills at the faucet and avoids spills. A built-in tank needs a spouted container and steady hands. If balance or grip is an issue, the removable tank is worth a lot. Test how you would fill it in your actual kitchen. Warm tap water also shortens the heating phase, so fill with warm water when the manual allows it. Never pour hot water above the limit the manual states, because a plastic tank and its seal are not built for boiling water.

Tank models still need a drain path for used water, and the tank itself must dry between loads. Standing water breeds odor, so a machine with an Air Refresh mode like the Comfee, or a drying stage, has an advantage. Open the lid and door after every use. Treat the tank as a food container that needs cleaning. A weekly rinse with a splash of white vinegar and a soft brush keeps film from building on the walls, and it is much easier than scrubbing a stained reservoir after a month of neglect.

A tank limits the load, so look for a place-setting claim rather than an item count. The Hermitlux states four place settings, while the Euhomy states 30 plus items and the Miniplus states a plate size. Compare dimensions, since all the cubes are about 16.5 to 17 inches on a side. If the stated capacity and the tank size seem out of proportion, trust the tank, because a small reservoir cannot feed an unlimited stack of dishes. Plan your loading around the water, not the rack.

Small tanks mean little water, so temperature matters. The Euhomy quotes 167 F and the Comfee Hygiene cycle reaches 158 F. Heat cleans grease but warps thin plastic. Check that the manual lists the hottest program and keep plastics away from it. Glass and ceramic handle high heat well, and baby bottles benefit from it, but lunch boxes and flexible containers do not. When in doubt, run a lower program and rely on a good pre-rinse.

A tank machine needs a power outlet and a drain hose that reaches a sink or bucket. The drain should end lower than the machine, or water will linger in the hose and smell. Keep the cord away from the pouring area. A stable, level counter keeps vibration low.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank volume
howWeEvaluated.description: We converted every tank to liters, so the Miniplus at 6 liters led and the Sunvivipro at about 4.5 liters trailed. A bigger tank scored better because it supports a fuller load.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fill and drain ease
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pouring, removable tanks and dual supply. The Sunvivipro's lift-out tank earned credit for easier filling, and dual-supply models earned credit for flexibility.

howWeEvaluated.title: Odor control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at drying stages and Air Refresh modes, with the Comfee's mode as the benchmark. Tanks are where odor starts, so these features carry weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored machines that state place settings, such as the Hermitlux at four. Item counts and missing figures earned less credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and program range
howWeEvaluated.description: We read hot-wash claims and program lists, with the Euhomy's 167 F and eight programs at the top. This is based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns.

cards.label: Built-in tank
cards.text: The Miniplus, Hermitlux, Euhomy, ChuMaste and original Comfee keep the tank in the body. You pour water in, which asks for a jug with a spout and a steady hand.

cards.label: Removable tank
cards.text: The Sunvivipro lifts its tank out so you fill it at the faucet. It is easier on the hands, but it adds a seal that must seat correctly every time.

howToChoose.note: Choose removable if pouring is a struggle, and built-in if you prefer fewer parts to lose.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A tank big enough for your usual load, a drain hose that reaches the sink and a tank that is easy to clean.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Miniplus is the strongest at 6 liters, while the Sunvivipro is the easiest to fill and the Hermitlux is the clearest about capacity.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want the largest tank and plate clearance, which means the Comfee Miniplus, or a removable tank, which means the Sunvivipro.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash one or two people's dishes. The ChuMaste covers that at the lowest cost.

maintenance.why: Standing water grows slime and odor. Dry the tank and leave the lid open.
Debris clogs the screen and weakens spray. A clean filter is the cheapest way to keep results consistent.
Removable tank only. A half-seated tank leaks, so look at the seal before closing the door.
Residue spreads odor. A damp gasket also weakens over time.
Use dishwasher cleaner to dissolve grease and scale. Never use hand soap.

faq.q: How much water does a tank dishwasher use per load?
faq.a: Roughly the size of the tank: about 4.5 to 6 liters across the six machines here. That is well below handwashing for a similar stack of dishes.
No. The two are the same, since 1.32 gallons is about 5 liters. Compare tank sizes in one unit to avoid being fooled.

faq.q: Can tank models run two loads in a row?
faq.a: Only after you refill. The tank holds one cycle's water, so a second load means a second fill. Plan on one or two cycles a day at most.

faq.q: How do I stop the tank from smelling?
faq.a: Empty it after use, dry it and leave the lid open. Machines with an Air Refresh mode, like the original Comfee, help with the chamber as well.

faq.q: Do I still need a drain?
faq.a: Yes. Used water leaves through a hose, which must run to a sink or bucket lower than the machine. A drain that climbs leaves water behind.

faq.q: Which one is best for dorm rooms?
faq.a: The ChuMaste and the original Comfee are the lowest in cost and the simplest. The Hermitlux fits if you want a stated four-setting capacity.
